feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear senior-level positioning, credible progression, and relevant digital strategy depth. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with limited quantified outcomes beyond scope metrics; a few style/grammar inconsistencies also reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in director and consulting roles, which strengthens credibility and leadership narrative.  
- Strong domain alignment: digital strategy, Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics, multimedia, and advocacy communications are consistently reinforced.  
- Good use of scale indicators such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers,” which adds impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: include results tied to traffic growth, engagement, conversion, efficiency, cost savings, or team performance, not just responsibilities and platform scope.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and save space.  
- Fix writing/style inconsistencies: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. other non-Oxford-comma lists); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper value proposition will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your seniority and strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and operational systems for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Reduce the long channel list; “multi-channel” or “cross-channel” already covers web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, editorial workflow design, and platform governance, with a strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, accessible content. Experienced in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and building scalable systems that improve execution across teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination also appear elsewhere; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinct will improve scanability and reduce repetition.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, sharper phrasing: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications • Web platform & CMS management • Editorial operations & governance • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow automation & systems design • Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional collaboration • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Replace “Multi-channel communication” with “Cross-channel communications” for more natural CV style.
- Change “Web & CMS administration” to “Web platform & CMS management” to sound more senior and strategic.
- Consider swapping in one more technical differentiator, such as “AI-enabled search” or “CMS modernization,” if targeting digital platform leadership roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Digital strategy & transformation” and several other items repeat Topline Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Make it sharper by emphasizing consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning in 2024.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, web modernization, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for member-facing communications.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one operations-improvement bullet.
- Rephrase task-heavy lines into outcomes: “Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular toolkit pages that improved launch speed/reusability” and “Led AI search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and UX.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains, stakeholder groups served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” substantially repeats the Director of Digital Media entry.
- Specific project details on AI search and microsites also duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this item higher-level.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with good scale metrics; it should read more like an executive achievement entry and less like a channel inventory. Emphasize transformation, team leadership, and business outcomes while trimming overlap with earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed enterprise digital communications strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, and budget for NACo’s web, email, social, and video ecosystem.”
- Combine the website bullets into one impact-led line: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel management bullet and add outcomes if available: newsletter open/click growth, audience growth, engagement rate, production volume, or cost savings from in-house video.
- Rephrase ops/analytics bullets to show decisions enabled: “Built reporting stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving leadership visibility and cross-team planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership and modernization.
- Video-program expansion may duplicate older NACo bullets unless framed here as building the in-house studio/capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around executional leadership, channel ownership, and concrete outputs that set up the promotion to Director.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial operations.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets around owned outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Recast coordination/workflow bullets with stronger verbs and, if possible, metrics: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing consistency and campaign coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “strengthened workflows/governance” too heavily; that theme is already stronger in the Director role.
- “Produced and expanded weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; distinguish this as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen the most senior, differentiating capabilities and use tighter phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with more specific, senior-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider dropping “leadership” from one line to avoid repetition and keep parallel structure.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this section more directly to scale in experience bullets rather than trying to show impact here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with the header and multiple NACo experience bullets; “audience-focused content planning” is the least distinctive item.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a list of tools to a tighter capability statement, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Remove lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially jQuery, unless it is essential for target roles.
- Prioritize the platforms most supported by recent experience; lead with Drupal and CMS modernization, and demote WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages if they are not central to current work.
- If space allows, make one phrase outcome-oriented: “API and workflow integrations supporting scalable publishing operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating it verbatim if possible.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a duplicate of the “Technical + IT” analytics section and misses the leadership/decision-making angle that better fits Topline Skills. Use this space to emphasize strategic analytics capability, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and measurement frameworks
- KPI design and executive reporting
- GA4, BigQuery, Power BI and Looker Studio dashboards
- User behavior insights, SEO and performance optimization
- Consider replacing “Microsoft Clarity” with “behavior analytics” unless Clarity is especially important for target roles.
- Tighten “Leadership reporting” to “executive reporting” or “decision-ready reporting.”
- If possible, align with outcomes from recent NACo work: analytics infrastructure, dashboarding, and improved strategic decision-making.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; Topline Skills should stay higher-level.
- Listing every tool here also overlaps with the Director of Digital Media bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with the Core Competencies line and several NACo bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and tied to recent in-house studio/event leadership rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from task list to capability scope: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end multimedia production”
- Tighten “Hybrid and virtual event production” to “Hybrid and virtual event delivery” for stronger operational ownership
- If space allows, add one differentiator tied to recent work: “In-house studio buildout and operations” or “Advocacy and event video programming”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one
- “Studio operations” and general video production are already evidenced in the Director of Digital Media role, so avoid repeating low-level execution language

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s generic and slightly redundant with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize platform depth/order rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider **Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** if brief qualifiers are allowed.
- If space permits, add one impact cue tied to recent work: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsite builds)** to reinforce seniority and scale.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use either **CMS platforms** or **Web Platforms & CMS**, but avoid mixing labels across sections.
- Consider trimming lower-signal items like **GitHub Pages** if you need room for stronger Drupal context.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- Drupal already appears multiple times in recent experience, so this section should complement with specificity, not repetition.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools that support recent delivery work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Implementation Tools**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in current consulting/Drupal work; if retained, place it last or mark it as legacy.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier in parentheses, e.g. **API integrations (content, analytics, workflow)** or **GitHub Actions (deployment automation)** to show application, not just familiarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates **“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”** in Topline Skills; keep the broader category there and let this section hold the more specific tools.
- **Google Tag Manager** may also partially overlap with the analytics section; keep it here only if positioned as implementation/tag deployment.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function and emphasize higher-value automation tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana • Slack/Teams”; move Basecamp and Trello to the end or cut if less current.
- Rename to sharpen positioning: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” or “Automation, Project & Collaboration Tools.”
- If space allows, group for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project ops: Jira, Asana, Basecamp, Trello | Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- If these tools drove measurable process improvements, reflect that in recent experience bullets instead of here; keep this line concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Jira, Asana, Basecamp, and Trello are similar category tools; listing all four may feel padded unless all are genuinely current.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since recent roles emphasize email operations and platform leadership, this item should signal level of use and avoid reading like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, journey automation)**
- If accurate, add stronger qualifiers tied to recent work: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • enterprise newsletter delivery • segmentation • automated journeys**
- Put the most current/relevant platform first; if Dynamics 365 is your newest or most strategic system, keep it first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; don’t repeat volume metrics here unless you remove them from experience.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item platform-specific rather than broad.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more concrete by emphasizing “firsts,” scope, and outputs, while keeping it clearly earlier-career than the 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and team-building: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and group channels: “...improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia production.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams/videos produced, publishing cadence, event audience, or team size.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while providing day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; if that later entry keeps ownership/expansion, this one should frame it as early production support or launch-stage work.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; use a more specific contribution if possible.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, innovation support, and the podcast as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with specific outputs if possible: web features, reports, multimedia explainers, stakeholder materials, etc.
- Add scope or results where available: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, internal teams served, or audience/engagement indicators.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so the CV reflects progression and gives more weight to recent leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; avoid repeating broad multimedia language here.
- Since podcast/video production appears elsewhere, position this as the origin point or first major multimedia initiative.
